newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-CLEMENS BACK ON WINNING TRACK AS JAYS BLANK ORIOLES.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-CLEMENS BACK ON WINNING TRACK AS JAYS BLANK ORIOLES.

text.p: Roger Clemens, Dan Plesac and Mike Timlin combined on a six-hitter and Joe Carter hit a two-run single to snap an eighth-inning tie as the Toronto Blue Jays blanked the Baltimore Orioles 3-0 Thursday.
Clemens (12-2) bounced back from his first two losses of the season and allowed just five singles over seven innings, walking two and striking out nine.

The win was his first since June 6. He joined the New York Mets' Bobby Jones as the major leagues' only 12-game winners. In his last two starts, both against Baltimore, Clemens has allowed no runs and nine hits in 14 innings, striking out 17.
He retired 13 straight batters between the second and sixth innings and struck out seven of 12 in one stretch.
"I never want to come out of a game," said Clemens. "I go all out every inning.
"Baltimore is a great ballclub. I was spent, but if the bullpen had been spent, I would have stayed out there."
Plesac got the first out in the eighth before Timlin got the final five outs for his seventh save.
The shutout, Toronto's league-leading eighth of the season, also snapped the Blue Jays' season-high five-game losing streak.
Scott Erickson (10-3) allowed two runs and four hits over seven innings.
After being the last team in baseball to be shut out, the Orioles have been blanked four times in the last eight games.
In Oakland, Mark McGwire tied a franchise record with his ninth career grand slam and Ariel Prieto remained unbeaten at home as the Athletics defeated the Texas Rangers 6-3.

Texas starter Julio Santana (3-3) surrendered singles to Jason McDonald and Rafael Bournigal in the bottom of the first and walked Geronimo Berroa before McGwire hit the next pitch over the left-centre fence for his 28th homer of the season.
McGwire broke the Oakland record for grand slams that he shared with Terry Steinbach and tied the Athletics franchise mark held by Jimmie Foxx and Sam Chapman.
Prieto (6-5) in seven starts at home is 5-0 with a 1.97 ERA. He is 1-5 on the road.
The Athletics won for just the second time in eight games. The Rangers lost for the eighth time in nine outings.
In Boston, Tony Clark had a pair of hits and three RBI and Phil Nevin added a pair of run-scoring doubles as the Detroit Tigers snapped the Red Sox' five-game winning streak 10-6.

Tigers starter Brian Moehler (5-6) notched the win despite allowing three solo homers, by Mike Stanley, John Valentin and Shane Mack. Three relievers combined to hold Boston to one run over the final 3 1/3 innings.
Red Sox starter Vaughn Eshelman (1-3) was tagged for five runs -- four earned -- and seven hits.
Boston was without outfielder Wil Cordero, who was a late scratch amid new revelations following his arrest earlier this month on domestic abuse charges.
In Seattle, Joey Cora, Jose Cruz Jr and Paul Sorrento homered and Jamie Moyer (7-2) won for the 17th time in his last 21 decisions as the Mariners beat the Anaheim Angels 6-3.
All three homers came off Angels starter Jason Dickson (8-4).
The loss was just the third in 13 division games for the Angels, who have split four meetings with the Mariners.
Seattle, which played without the injured Ken Griffey Jr, has won seven of eight overall and 10 of 11 at the Kingdome. Griffey sat out with tightness in his right hamstring.
In Kansas City, Jeff King delivered a two-run single and Chili Davis hit a two-run homer in a four-run fourth inning as the Royals rallied for a 4-3 win over the Milwaukee Brewers.

Chris Haney (1-2) gave up both runs and six hits over six innings with a season-high six strikeouts. Ricky Bones, in his first appearance with Kansas City, allowed one run over 2 1/3 innings before Jeff Montgomery got the last two outs.
Jose Mercedes (3-3) took the loss despite pitching his first career complete game.
Gerald Williams homered for Milwaukee, which has lost four of its last five games.

At Minnesota, the Chicago White Sox moved above the .500 mark for the first time since Opening Day as Mike Cameron homered twice and Frank Thomas and Harold Baines each drove in three runs in an 11-1 rout of the Twins.

James Baldwin (5-8) beat the Twins for the second time in six days, limiting them to one run and five hits in seven innings. Chuck McElroy retired the last six batters as Chicago extended its winning streak to six games.
The White Sox have won eight of their last nine games and are at 38-37.
Minnesota starter LaTroy Hawkins (1-2) suffered his second straight loss, both against Chicago.
